model_summary: Monthly workforce, hires, fires, in-house production, overtime hours, outsourcing, sales, end inventory and backorders; maximize sales revenue minus material, outsourcing, holding, backorder, regular wage (paid on all 160 h per worker), overtime, hiring and firing costs; labor-hour, overtime-cap (20 h/worker), inventory/backorder balance and terminal conditions.
type_rationale: Workers, units and hires/fires are integer counts while overtime hours are continuous; all constraints and the objective are linear.
notes: Units (tables, inventory, outsourcing) treated as integer as well as workers; all-continuous version gives integer_relaxed_objective (then type would be LP). Workforce in month t is after that month's hiring/firing. Revenue counts all units delivered (total equals total demand since backorders must be cleared).

model_summary: Grams of each of 7 foods (continuous) plus selection binaries; maximize fiber; total 600 g, cost <= $15, exactly one protein selected, at least two vegetables selected, amount <= 600*selection.
type_rationale: Continuous gram amounts with 0-1 selection variables linked by big-M; linear objective and constraints.
notes: Proteins have no fiber, so the optimum selects a protein with 0 g (and two extra vegetables selected at 0 g); no minimum purchase amount is given, so selection is only an upper-bound link. Requiring a strictly positive protein amount would make the supremum unattained but equal to the same value.

model_summary: Integer weekly output of shirts, short-sleeves, casual clothes plus binary equipment-use variables; maximize (price - variable cost)*quantity minus fixed equipment cost of used lines; labor <= 1500, material <= 1600.
type_rationale: Integer product quantities and 0-1 fixed-charge variables with linear constraints (MILP if quantities taken as continuous).

model_summary: Integer number of salespeople starting at each of 6 shift times; minimize total; each 4-hour period covered by the two overlapping shifts meets its requirement (cyclic).
type_rationale: Integer headcounts, linear covering constraints and objective.

model_summary: Hours of each workshop assigned to each component plus number of complete products z; maximize z; workshop hour capacities and each component's total output >= z.
type_rationale: Continuous hours and product count z (max-min objective via epigraph is already linear); problem asks for an LP formulation.
notes: Number of complete products is fractional at the LP optimum; problem explicitly asks for an LP so it is kept continuous.

model_summary: Monthly purchase, sales and end inventory Jul-Dec; maximize sales revenue minus purchase cost; stock after start-of-month purchase <= 500, inventory balance from 200 initial units.
issue_note: Timing of sales vs purchases ('purchases are made at the beginning of each month'): whether goods bought at the start of a month can be sold in the same month (main) or sales in a month are limited to stock carried in from the previous month.

readings.reading: Purchased goods can be sold in the same month; stock after purchase <= 500.
Sales in month t limited to stock carried into month t (before purchase); stock after purchase <= 500.

type_rationale: Continuous purchase/sale quantities, linear balance and capacity constraints and linear objective.
notes: Integer requirement immaterial (LP optimum integral). Ending inventory has no salvage value.

model_summary: Integer regular and contract nurses starting at each of 6 shift times; minimize total pay (8 h * 10 or 15 yuan); cyclic coverage of each period's requirement.
type_rationale: Integer nurse counts; linear coverage constraints and linear cost.
notes: The question asks whether/how many contract nurses to hire: the optimum hires 0 contract nurses (asked_value), objective is the minimum total pay. No limit on regular nurses is given; the question appears to be a sub-part of a longer exercise.

model_summary: Binary take/not-take for 6 children; minimize cost; 3 to 4 children, Ginny taken, Harry excludes Fred and George, George requires Fred and Hermione.
type_rationale: All 0-1 variables with linear logical constraints.

model_summary: Binary purchase of 4 restaurants; maximize annual revenue; total cost <= 6 million; D excludes A.
type_rationale: All 0-1 variables, linear budget and conflict constraints.

model_summary: Integer production of high/mid/low-end toys; maximize profit; labor <= 1000 h, inspection <= 500 h, demand caps 50/80/150.
type_rationale: Integer unit counts with linear constraints and objective.
notes: LP relaxation gives the same value.

model_summary: Tons shipped from yards A,B to 3 areas; minimize ton-km; demands met exactly; A ships at least 80 t and B at least 100 t (all received coal distributed).
issue_note: 'each receiving no less than 80 tons and 100 tons': main reading = each yard must distribute at least that much (total exactly matches demand 180 t, so supplies are 80/100); alternative = these are only lower bounds on availability with no upper limit, so supply is effectively uncapacitated.

readings.reading: 80/100 are lower bounds on availability only; no supply limit.

type_rationale: Continuous shipment quantities, linear transportation constraints and objective.
notes: Treating 80/100 as upper capacities gives the same value as the main reading since total equals demand.

model_summary: Goal programming: total full-time hours x1 and part-time hours x2 with deviation variables; lexicographic P1 min sales shortfall below 5500 pairs (5x1+2x2), P2 min under-employment below 800 / 320 h, P3 min overtime hours above 800 / 320 h.
issue_note: The task only asks to 'establish a model'; no single numeric objective is defined. Reported value is the P3 level (overtime hours) after P1 and P2 are fully met; P3 could also be weighted by overtime pay (1.5 vs 0.7). Wages and the 0.3 profit per pair are not used by the goals as stated.
type_rationale: Continuous hours and deviation variables; each priority level is a linear program (preemptive goal programming).
notes: P1 and P2 deviations both reach 0; overtime is all full-time (172 h) in both readings.

model_summary: Packs of Meaties and Yummies; maximize price minus grain, meat and mixing costs; grains <= 400,000 lb, meat <= 300,000 lb, Meaties <= 90,000 packs.
type_rationale: Continuous pack quantities, linear constraints and linear profit.
notes: Unit profits 0.65 and 0.45 per pack; LP optimum is integral.

model_summary: Integer numbers of packages A and B; maximize revenue 30A+50B; shirts A+3B <= 200, pants 2A+B <= 100, A >= 20, B >= 10.
type_rationale: Integer package counts with linear constraints and objective.
notes: LP relaxation gives the same value.

model_summary: All feasible cutting patterns enumerated (<=5 pieces, leftover <=100 mm); integer pipes per pattern in 4 rank slots with binary slot assignment; minimize raw pipes plus rank-based extra cost (k/10 pipe value per pipe for the k-th most used pattern); demands met; at most 4 patterns.
issue_note: 'the most frequently used cutting pattern incurs an extra cost equal to 1/10 of the value of one raw pipe...': main reading = extra cost per raw pipe cut with that pattern; alternative = one-time cost per pattern used.

readings.reading: Extra k/10 pipe value per pipe cut with the k-th most used pattern.
Extra k/10 pipe value charged once per pattern used.

type_rationale: The direct model has integer pieces-per-pattern times integer pipe counts and frequency-rank costs; with bounded integers it is exactly linearized by pattern enumeration and binary slot assignment (rearrangement makes free slot assignment equal to rank ordering), giving a pure IP.
notes: Costs expressed in units of one raw pipe's value (value not given numerically). Overproduction allowed (demand >= order).

model_summary: Binary arc variables for an asymmetric-form 4-city tour with MTZ subtour elimination; minimize travel cost; each city entered and left once.
